$comment: Configuration for scripts/figma/compare-ui.mjs and harvest-ui.mjs (Plan 217). `components` says how to render each Figma set in Storybook: the story, the element to measure, and how a Figma variant's properties become story args (`args`: Figma property to arg name; `values`: Figma value to arg value, where they differ) and interactions (`state`: hover and pressed are made by the harvester). `allow` lists differences the owner accepted, each with a reason; an entry that matches nothing fails the run.

allow.reason: Figma draws a fixed 240px frame; in code the input is w-full and takes its container (320px in the story). Width is layout, not look.
Code shows the placeholder attribute, which is not a text node; Figma draws a text layer so the placeholder can be edited and styled.
Both hug their content now (padding, gap and type match). The story card holds different copy than the Figma placeholder content, so its height differs.
Figma draws a fixed 240px frame; in code the textarea is w-full and takes its container (384px in the story). Width is layout, not look.
Code shows the placeholder attribute, which is not a text node; Figma draws a text layer so the placeholder can be edited and styled.
Figma draws a fixed 400px frame; in code the alert is w-full and takes its container.
Code positions the icon absolutely beside the text (no flex gap); Figma uses an auto-layout gap of alert.gap to place the icon, the result looks the same.
The story wraps the bar in a shrink-wrapped box, so w-full measures 0; Figma draws a 240px track.
Follows from the 0px width in the story: the radius is clamped to half the width. The token (4px) matches Figma.
Figma draws a fixed 240px slider (the range is half of it, 120px); in code the slider is w-full and takes its container (300px in the story, the range 150px). The 50% proportion matches.
The Figma root is a 24px wrapper sized to the thumb; the UI root is the 8px track row and the 24px thumb overflows it. Track, range and thumb sizes each match.

Open (owner decision): Figma rounds the range to 4px, so its trailing end is rounded; in code the range has no radius and only the track's overflow clips it, so the end at the thumb is square (hidden behind the thumb).

The only default-variant story with an action (toast--with-action) renders a title, description and action but no close button; Figma draws all of them, so the height differs by 3px. Recheck if a default story with a close is added.
The UI label is an inline element holding the story copy ("Email Address"); Figma draws the word Label. Width follows the copy.
An inline label measures its font content area (22px at md), not its line height; the text layer line height matches.
Figma gap 4 sits between the label and the optional required indicator, which is hidden here; the UI label is inline text.
Figma draws a fixed 200px trigger; in code the trigger is w-full and takes its container (320px in the story).
Figma draws a fixed 240px line; in code the separator is w-full.
The Separator story renders horizontally only, so the vertical variant is not rendered by this run and measures 0.
The story forces className w-48 h-4, so the size and variant axes are overridden; Figma draws the token sizes.
The story forces className w-48 h-4, so the size and variant axes are overridden; Figma draws the token sizes.
Follows from the story forcing w-48 h-4: the radius is clamped to half the 16px height. The Figma radius is the token.
The UI pulses; the measurement catches a frame mid-animation (0.86 to 0.88). Figma draws the resting 1.
Figma fills the avatar root with the fallback background; the UI root has avatar.background under a full-size fallback of the same size, so the visible result is the fallback color.
The story gives AvatarFallback no size, so its text stays at md (14px); the component scales it when size is passed (avatar.fallback font-size tokens), which is what Figma draws.
Same as font size: the story keeps the md fallback line height.
Figma draws a 280px field; in code the form is w-full (512px in the story).
The UI separates label, input and helper with margins on the field wrapper, not a flex gap; Figma uses an auto-layout gap of 8.
An inline label measures its font content area (22px), not its 16px line height; same as the Label set.
Code shows the placeholder attribute, which is not a text node; Figma draws a text layer.
Figma items hug a letter (28 to 34px); the UI items are fixed 40px squares holding an icon, so the group is wider.
The vertical story draws more items than the Figma placeholder (three 40px rows).
Figma draws the letters B, I and U; the story draws icons (svg), which are not text nodes.
The vertical story has no pressed item first, so its first text is the unpressed colour; Figma's first row is the pressed one.
Figma draws a fixed or hugging width; in code the element takes its container or the story copy, so width is layout, not look.
Figma draws only the header row (21px); the UI root includes the header, a bordered item and the content area.
The UI header row is story-authored with 16px side padding; Figma has none.
Open (owner decision): Figma draws the collapsible root with a 4px radius and a #0b0806 fill; the UI Collapsible renders no box of its own (the story header is story-authored).
Open (owner decision): see the radius entry; the UI Collapsible has no root fill.
Open (owner decision): Figma draws the header Regular; the story's header is a 600 weight h4, authored in the story, not the component.
The UI scrollbar spans the 286px viewport and the thumb is proportional to the content (76px); Figma draws a 200px bar with a 40px thumb.
Open (owner decision): the UI thumb is 5px wide (a 10px track with 2.5px inset); Figma draws an 8px thumb in an 8px track.
Open (owner decision): the UI track is rounded (4px) and the thumb radius follows its 5px width (2.5px); Figma has an unrounded track and a 4px thumb radius.
Figma draws a fixed or hugging width; in code the element takes its container or the story copy, so width is layout, not look.
The UI nav wraps the ol (the flex row); Figma's root is the row, so its gap of 4 has no counterpart on the nav element.
The UI link carries a 4px radius for its focus ring; Figma draws it square.

Open (owner decision, probable UI bug): BreadcrumbPage sets aria-disabled="true", so its aria-disabled:text-(--color-breadcrumb-link-disabled) class wins over --color-breadcrumb-current and the current page renders #b19f89 instead of Figma's #f9f7f5.
Figma draws a fixed or hugging width; in code the element takes its container or the story copy, so width is layout, not look.
Figma draws the empty state (109px: search row and the empty message); the UI root is the whole command palette with its list (326px), and the empty message carries 24px padding.
The UI empty message has 24px vertical padding; Figma sets the height on the frame instead.
The UI search row is not a flex container (the icon has its own margin); Figma uses a gap of 8.
Code shows the placeholder attribute, which is not a text node; Figma draws a text layer.
The story passes className="rounded-lg" (8px), which tailwind-merge lets replace the component's own radius (--space-command-content-radius, border-radius.md = 4px, the value Figma draws).

The story passes className="border", a 1px border the component's root does not have (the component draws only the search row's bottom rule, which the harvester does not read: it measures the top edge). Figma draws none on the root, like the component.

The story passes className="shadow-md", Tailwind's 10% black shadow; the component's root has no shadow of its own (it sits inside a popover or dialog). Figma draws shadow/md on its overlay surface, which is 40% black in dark. The two shadows are not meant to match.
Open (owner decision): the UI Previous link is 100.81px (8px left padding), Figma 109px (16px); the row is 356px in the UI, 328px in Figma.
The UI nav wraps the ul (the flex row); Figma's root is the row, so its gap of 4 has no counterpart on the nav element.

Open (owner decision): the UI Previous link is padded 8px on the icon side where Figma has 16px; the page links are fixed 40px squares with 16px padding in the UI and none in Figma (the box is the same size).
Figma draws a fixed or hugging width; in code the element takes its container or the story copy, so width is layout, not look.
The UI list and panel are spaced by margin on the panel, not a flex gap; Figma uses a gap of 16.
Open (owner decision): the UI tab list is padded 4px on all sides; Figma has 4px left and right only.

Open (owner decision): Figma strokes the active tab (#416975) and the list (#4e453d); the UI active tab has no border colour and the list border is on the bottom edge only, which the harvester does not read.
Open (owner decision): the UI inactive tab is 33px tall (like the active one); Figma draws it 29px.
Figma draws the tab list and one line of content (160px); the UI root is the story's whole form (260px), and the panel holds story fields.
The story's tab panel starts with a 16px label; Figma's panel text is 14px.
The story's tab panel starts with a 16px label; Figma's panel text has a 21px line height.
Figma draws a fixed or hugging width; in code the element takes its container or the story copy, so width is layout, not look.

Open (owner decision): the closed Figma accordion is 56px (a 40px row plus 16px); the UI item is 42px (40px trigger plus borders). The Figma trigger is the 16px text where the UI trigger is the 40px button.
Padding sits on the row in Figma (12px) and on the trigger button in the UI.
